assertion.text: Erdős Problem #730: declared status 'open'. Formalized: yes. Are there infinitely many pairs of integers $n\neq m$ such that $\binom{2n}{n}$ and $\binom{2m}{m}$ have the same set of prime divisors? Current best: It is not known whether there are such pairs of the shape $(n,n+k)$ for every $k\geq 1$. Prize: no. OEIS: A129515. Tags: base representations, binomial coefficients, number theory.
